content_units: You are disputing   £600 total deductions   from a   £1,200 deposit  :
- emails showing the carpet stains existed before move-in
This is an evidence-and-process task, so the goal is to build a clean file showing   pre-existing condition, fair wear and tear, and proof gaps in the landlord’s claim  .

1. Build the file   Gather everything in one place   Save tenancy agreement; deposit protection details; check-in/out reports; dated photos; stain-related emails; landlord deduction message   One folder with dated PDFs/images

2. Map the facts   Link each deduction to evidence   Create 2 sections: carpet cleaning and repainting; note what condition existed at move-in vs move-out; flag normal wear and tear   One-page issue summary

3. Request proof in writing   Make landlord justify the charges   Ask for invoices/quotes; cleaning/redecoration evidence; check-in/check-out comparisons; age/condition of carpet/paint; calculation method   Written request email sent

4. Review reasonableness   Test whether the sums look supported   Check if charges are for betterment; compare against lifespan/use; see whether full-room repainting is being claimed for minor marks   Annotated comments on each charge

5. Start formal dispute   Use deposit scheme process if unresolved   Confirm scheme; submit evidence before deadline; upload photos, emails, tenancy docs, chronology, and written challenge   Formal dispute submission
6. Keep a record trail   Preserve a clean timeline   Save all replies; log dates sent/received; avoid phone-only discussions; confirm verbal points by email   Final case log
What to Gather for Each Deduction
- Move-in photos showing the carpet condition
- Emails/messages proving stains were already present before move-in
- Any clause in the tenancy agreement about cleaning standards at check-out
- Proof the carpet was returned in broadly similar condition apart from fair use
- Lack of professional evidence that cleaning was actually needed
- Evidence that the landlord is trying to charge for improvement rather than restoration
- Is the landlord claiming for   all carpet cleaning   or only a specific room?
- Is there evidence the carpet was cleaner at move-in than at move-out?
- Does the amount look like a real cost, or just a round figure?
- Any evidence of existing scuffs, marks, nail holes, or aged paint at move-in
- Tenancy length and any notes showing ordinary day-to-day use
- Marks consistent with   fair wear and tear
- No proof of unusual damage beyond normal occupation
- No evidence of age/condition of paint before the tenancy
- No explanation why   full repainting   was necessary
- Is the claim for one wall, one room, or multiple rooms?
- Are the alleged marks minor enough that they may be ordinary wear?
- Is the landlord charging full redecoration cost without allowing for prior age and use?
Written Requests to Send the Landlord or Agent
Send one clear email asking for the following in writing:
- A full itemised breakdown of the proposed deductions
- Copies of any invoices, receipts, or contractor quotes for:
- The dated photos relied on for the deductions
- why the issue is beyond fair wear and tear
- how the amount claimed was calculated
- The age and condition at tenancy start of:
- Whether any allowance has been made for:
- Confirmation of the tenancy deposit protection scheme used and the reference number, if you do not already have it
- “Please treat this as a request for the evidence relied on for the proposed deposit deductions.”
- “Please identify the specific damage alleged, the room/location, and the basis on which you say this exceeds fair wear and tear.”
- “Please explain how the sums claimed avoid betterment.”
- “Please confirm whether the carpet staining you rely on is said to be different from the staining shown in the pre-tenancy emails and move-in photographs.”
Practical Timeline From the 2025-08-31 Tenancy End
Given the tenancy ended on   2025-08-31  , use this practical sequence:
- Export all photos with visible dates if possible
- Gather the stain-related emails into one PDF
- Write your issue summary for carpet and repainting
- Ask for scheme details if missing
- Compare check-in and move-out material side by side
- Highlight any mismatch between claimed damage and move-in condition
- Raise the dispute with the relevant tenancy deposit scheme
- Upload only the strongest, organised evidence
- Present a short chronology rather than long arguments
- pre-existing carpet stains documented by email
